To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rabbit, pig and human angiogenins have similar three-dimensional structures and are similar in their ability to bind to placental RNase inhibitor.

the angiogenins of rabbit, pig, and mouse, like the human angiogenin and other RNases, are homologous proteins with a common three-dimensional structure, and that the angiogenic and second-messenger activities of angiogenin are due to the interaction of this protein with a receptor that is different from the ribonuclease-inhibitor protein and the 28S rRNA.
rabbit, pig and human angiogenins are structurally related proteins that have been purified and characterized, and that the sequences of the first three of these proteins are known.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and sequence of rabbit, pig, and mouse angiogenin.
the identification of the residues and regions of angiogenin that are functionally important.
the identification of residues and regions that are important in the function of the angiogenins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
angiogenins are ribonucleases that are capable of inducing neovascularization and of inhibiting protein synthesis, and that these activities are mediated by the same molecule.

angiogenin is an RNase that is not a ribonucleolytically active enzyme, and that it has been adapted for its angiogenic function by acquiring a new function and by losing its ribonucleolytical activity.
the angiogenin protein is an RNase that is a potent angiogenic factor, a potent inhibitor for protein synthesis, and a weak RNase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
angiogenins are a new family of proteins that are related to the ribonucleases but are functionally different.

angiogenin is a protein that is highly conserved in evolution, has the catalytic properties of an RNase, and is a protein with several activities, some of which may not be related to its catalytic activity.

the angiogenin family of proteins, like the pancreatic RNases, is comprised of proteins that share a common structure but have different functions and different mechanisms for exerting those functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angiogenins are members of a family of proteins that are related in sequence to the RNases, but which have evolved to perform different functions.
angiogenins and RNases have a common ancestry, but that angiogenins are not simply modified RNases.
angiogenesis is a very ancient process and has been conserved throughout the evolution of mammals.
